# The session domain

The one running sketch a host holds: opening it, pinning what a repeatable run needs pinned, photographing it, reading back what its last frame cost, and evaluating text inside it.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Namespace in the definition | sigil.protocol.session |
| What a host implements | `sigil::protocol::session::SessionAgent`, mounted by `sigil::protocol::session::wire` |
| C++ client | `sigil::protocol::session::SessionClient` |
| Events sent through | `sigil::protocol::session::SessionEvents` |
| Python client | sigil.protocol.session.Session |

## Commands

### session.open

Opens a sketch by registry name or by path, replacing the session open, and answers once it is set up: under the wall's clock once its first frame is drawn, and under any other with no frame drawn, so that the first frame is the client's first step, as a plate's is.

In Python, Session.open.

Answered later, through the reply the agent is handed, once the work is done.

Takes `OpenParameters`: What open is asked.

| Parameter | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sketch` | string, required | "" | A registry name, or the path to a sketch file or directory, which is compiled and loaded as a person's edit would be. |
| `kind` | string | "" | The runtime to open it through, scene2d or scene3d; empty for whichever it declares. |

Answers `Summary`: A session as a list shows it.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sketch` | string | "" | The registry name, or the path, it was opened from. |
| `kind` | string | "" | The runtime it draws through: scene2d or scene3d. |
| `width` | float | 0.0 | The canvas width it declared, in canvas units. |
| `height` | float | 0.0 | The canvas height it declared, in canvas units. |
| `moment` | double | -1.0 | The moment it declared it is photographed at, in seconds; negative where it declared none. |

### session.pinDevice

Pins the device the session draws with.

In Python, Session.pinDevice.

Answered at once.

Takes `DeviceParameters`: What pinDevice is asked.

| Parameter | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `device` | Device (enumeration) | Cpu | The device the session draws with from now on. |

Answers nothing but that it was done.

### session.pinDensity

Pins the density every raster the session bakes is formed at, from the first frame of each session opened after it and from now on in the one open. A still at that density of a session pinned before it opened is the plate a sweep takes of the same moment; a bake formed before the pin is formed again only when its node describes again.

In Python, Session.pinDensity.

Answered at once.

Takes `DensityParameters`: What pinDensity is asked.

| Parameter | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `density` | double | 0.0 | Device pixels per canvas unit every raster the session bakes is formed at; zero for the density a plate of the session is photographed at. |

Answers nothing but that it was done.

### session.still

Photographs the session at the clock as it stands, as a plate is taken: a runtime that re-renders its still at the still's size draws one frame of no length more to do it, so the clock stays at the moment photographed. A clock that is held — paused, or by the Pause policy — photographs the frame it holds as it was last drawn, drawing nothing new, so two stills under it are one picture.

In Python, Session.still.

Answered later, through the reply the agent is handed, once the work is done.

Takes `StillParameters`: What still is asked.

| Parameter | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `density` | double | 1.0 | Device pixels per canvas unit. |
| `path` | string | "" | Where the still is written, under the state root; empty for a name the host picks. |

Answers `StillResult`: The still, written.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | "" | Where it was written. |
| `width` | uint | 0 | Its width in pixels. |
| `height` | uint | 0 | Its height in pixels. |
| `seconds` | double | 0.0 | Clock seconds of the moment it shows. |

### session.sequence

Photographs frames one after another, stepping the clock one frame of the rate between them. Refused unless the clock's policy is Advance.

In Python, Session.sequence.

Answered later, through the reply the agent is handed, once the work is done.

Takes `SequenceParameters`: What sequence is asked.

| Parameter | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `frames` | uint | 1 | Frames to photograph, one after another. |
| `rate` | double | 60.0 | Frames per second the clock advances between them. |
| `density` | double | 1.0 | Device pixels per canvas unit. |
| `directory` | string | "" | The directory the frames are written into, under the state root; empty for one the host picks. |

Answers `SequenceResult`: The frames, written.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `paths` | list of string | empty | Where each frame was written, in order. |
| `width` | uint | 0 | Each frame's width in pixels. |
| `height` | uint | 0 | Each frame's height in pixels. |

How the last frame split.

### session.profile

Attributes what the next frame spends to what spent it, and answers the most expensive rows once that frame is drawn.

**Experimental**: its shape may still change.

In Python, Session.profile.

Answered later, through the reply the agent is handed, once the work is done.

Takes `ProfileParameters`: What profile is asked.

| Parameter | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | uint | 12 | The most rows to answer. |

Answers `ProfileResult`: What the profiled frame spent, the most expensive first.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rows` | list of string | empty | Each row in the runtime's own words: what spent the time, and how much. |

### session.evaluate

Runs text in the running sketch's own namespace, between two of its frames, on the thread that draws them, and answers what it evaluated to, what it printed and what it raised. Names the sketch's module binds are in scope, beside the running sketch as `self` and its context as `ctx`. Text that ran to its end describes the sketch again — a sketch that declares its tree is asked for it again — so the next frame shows the change; text that raised changes nothing more, and the sketch runs on. A sketch compiled ahead of time evaluates nothing and refuses it. A host opens this door only when it is told to, and refuses it otherwise, because it runs whatever a client sends.

**Experimental**: its shape may still change.

In Python, Session.evaluate.

Answered later, through the reply the agent is handed, once the work is done.

Takes `EvaluateParameters`: What evaluate is asked.

| Parameter | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | string, required | "" | The source text, in the language the running sketch is written in. |
| `mode` | EvaluationMode (enumeration) | Expression | Whether the text is one expression or statements. |

Answers `EvaluateResult`: What an evaluation answered.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | string | "" | The expression's value as the language represents it; empty for statements and where the text raised. |
| `output` | string | "" | What the text wrote to the standard output and the standard error while it ran, in the order written. |
| `error` | EvaluationError (table) | absent | What the text raised; absent where it ran to its end. |

### session.pointer

Puts the pointer over the running sketch at a point on its canvas, with its button down or up, as a person's pointer is: the sketch reads it from its next frame on, and a sketch of input hooks calls the one the change from its last frame names.

In Python, Session.pointer.

Answered at once.

Takes `PointerParameters`: What pointer is asked.

| Parameter | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x` | float | 0.0 | Where the pointer stands across the canvas, in the canvas units the sketch declared. |
| `y` | float | 0.0 | Where it stands down the canvas, in the canvas units the sketch declared. |
| `pressed` | bool | false | Whether its button is down. |

Answers nothing but that it was done.

### session.key

A key going down or up over the running sketch, as a person's keyboard sends one: the sketch reads it from its next frame on.

In Python, Session.key.

Answered at once.

Takes `KeyParameters`: What key is asked.

| Parameter | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string, required | "" | The key's name as a keyboard spells it: "a", "ArrowLeft", "Enter". |
| `code` | int | 0 | The key's code. |
| `pressed` | bool | false | Whether it went down; false when it went up. |

Answers nothing but that it was done.

### session.enable

Starts this client's session events.

In Python, Session.enable.

Answered by the dispatcher itself, never by the agent: it starts or stops this client's session events.

### session.disable

Stops this client's session events.

In Python, Session.disable.

Answered by the dispatcher itself, never by the agent: it starts or stops this client's session events.

## Events

What the session tells a client that enabled it.

### session.opened

A session opened, by a client or by a person.

In Python, Session.onOpened.

Carries `OpenedEvent`: A session opened.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `summary` | Summary (table), required | absent | The session. |

### session.closed

The session closed.

In Python, Session.onClosed.

Carries `ClosedEvent`: A session closed.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sketch` | string | "" | The registry name, or the path, it was opened from. |

### session.failed

A session could not be opened, or rebuilt after an edit.

In Python, Session.onFailed.

Carries `FailedEvent`: A session could not be opened, or could not be rebuilt after an edit.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sketch` | string | "" | The registry name, or the path, it was asked for. |
| `message` | string | "" | What stopped it, in the compiler's or the runtime's own words. |

## Types

### Device

What a session draws with.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Cpu` | Skia's raster backend: the reference every plate is judged against. |
| `Gpu` | The GPU, through the host's device. |

### EvaluationMode

How evaluate reads the text it is sent.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Expression` | One expression, whose value is answered. |
| `Statements` | Statements, run for what they do; the value answered is empty. |

### EvaluationError

What stopped an evaluation: the exception the text raised, in the language's own words.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | string | "" | The exception's type, by its name. |
| `message` | string | "" | The exception's message. |
| `traceback` | string | "" | The traceback, as the language prints it, from the evaluated text down. |

### LaneCost

What one lane of a frame cost, named by the runtime that spent it.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | "" | The lane, in the runtime's own word. |
| `milliseconds` | double | 0.0 | Milliseconds it spent. |

### MeasuredValue

One number a sketch measured about its own execution.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | "" | The name the sketch gave it. |
| `value` | double | 0.0 | The value it measured. |
| `pinned` | double | 0.0 | The value a repeatable run shows in its place. |
